'''Kelly Tyler Olynyk''' ({{IPAc-en|oʊ|ˈ|l|ɪ|n|ᵻ|k}} {{respell|oh|LIN|ik}}; born April 19, 1991) is a Canadian professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[San Antonio Spurs]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) and the captain of the [[Canada men's national basketball team]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga Bulldogs]], where he earned [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] honors in 2013.

After forgoing his senior season, Olynyk was selected by the [[Dallas Mavericks]] with the 13th overall pick in the [[2013 NBA draft]] before being immediately traded to the [[Boston Celtics]]. He spent four seasons with the team, helping them reach the [[Eastern Conference Finals]] in 2017. During the 2017 off-season, Olynyk signed with the [[Miami Heat]], with whom he reached the [[2020 NBA Finals]]. He was traded to the [[Houston Rockets]] in March 2021.

Olynyk signed with the [[Detroit Pistons]] during the 2021 off-season, and was traded to the [[Utah Jazz]] during the 2022 off-season. He spent two seasons with the team before being traded to the [[Toronto Raptors]] during the 2023–24 season, and then to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] during the 2024–25 season. Olynyk joined the Spurs during the 2025 off-season, with whom he reached the [[2026 NBA Finals]].

==Early life==
Olynyk was born on April 19, 1991, in [[Toronto]], Ontario, where he began playing basketball at an early age. Alongside future NBA player [[Cory Joseph]], he played for the Scarborough Blues, a rep basketball team that rarely lost from the late 1990s to the early 2000s. One defeat came against rival Toronto 5-0, a rep team from the city's west end led by [[Stephen Curry]].<ref name="toronto">{{cite web|first=David|last=Ebner|title=Canada's quest for elite basketball status begins in Toronto|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/sports/basketball/for-canada-the-story-of-the-quest-for-elite-basketball-status-begins-in-toronto/article26130354/|work=[[The Globe and Mail]]|date=August 28, 2015|access-date=February 1, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Grange |first=Michael |date=February 14, 2015 |title=Curry’s path to NBA stardom forged in Toronto |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/basketball/nba/currys-path-to-nba-stardom-forged-in-toronto/ |access-date=October 17, 2025 |website=Sportsnet.ca}}</ref> Olynyk moved with his family to [[Kamloops]], [[British Columbia]], when he was in seventh grade.<ref name=thestar>{{cite web|first=Nicholas K.|last=Geranios|url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/basketball/2013/01/15/kelly_olynyk_emerges_as_star_for_no_8_gonzaga_mens_basketball_team.html|title=Kelly Olynyk emerges as star for No. 8 Gonzaga men's basketball team|work=Toronto Star|date=January 15, 2013|access-date=January 15, 2013}}</ref>

==High school career==
Olynyk did not attend a high school or prep school in the [[United States]]; instead, he stayed home at [[South Kamloops Secondary School]]. He gained exposure to U.S. competition and coaches by playing on provincial teams, competing in [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) and non-AAU tournaments in the U.S., and representing the Canadian junior national team.<ref name="Anderson">{{cite magazine |last=Anderson |first=Kelli |date=March 18, 2013 |title=Canada's Got Talent |url=https://www.si.com/vault/2013/03/18/106298102/canadas-got-talent |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230414173605/https://vault.si.com/vault/2013/03/18/canadas-got-talent |archive-date=April 14, 2023 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]}}</ref> Olynyk developed as a [[point guard]], continuing to play that position even after growing from 6'3" (1.90 m) to 6'10" (2.08 m) in [[Education in Canada#Canada outside Quebec|grade 11]].<ref name=Anderson/> He was heavily recruited out of high school by programs likes [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]], [[Providence Friars men's basketball|Providence]], and [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|North Carolina State]]. Ultimately, he chose [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]], in part so he could play closer to home.<ref name="thestar" />

Olynyk was named Basketball BC's ''Outstanding High School Player of the Year'' in his senior season, leading his South Kamloops Titans to a 36–2 record and a third-place finish at the BC AAA High School Boys' Basketball Championships.<ref name=bio>{{cite web |url=http://www.gozags.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=26400&ATCLID=205173776 |title=Kelly Olynyk Biography |work=GoZags.com |access-date=July 7, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130522185003/http://www.gozags.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=26400&ATCLID=205173776 |archive-date=May 22, 2013 }}</ref>

Olynyk also played quarterback for the Titans and broke his arm during a playoff game in 2007.<ref name="bio" />

==College career==
[[File: Kelly Olynyk v USD Toreros.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Olynyk at Gonzaga]]

Olynyk played [[college basketball]] at [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]] from 2009 to 2013. He was mostly a bench player for the Bulldogs in his freshman and sophomore years, averaging around 12 to 13 minutes per game. In order to improve his game and get stronger, Gonzaga and Olynyk agreed that he would [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] his junior year (2011–12), meaning he would practice with the team, but not play.

Olynyk returned to the Bulldogs lineup for the first game of the 2012–13 season, and had a great season, being selected as a [[2013 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|Consensus First-Team All-American]], as well as to the 2012–13 [[Academic All-America]] first team.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.gozags.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=26400&ATCLID=206473761 |title=Olynyk Named To Capital One Academic All-America Team |work=GoZags.com |date=February 21, 2013 |access-date=May 17, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131103182848/http://www.gozags.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=26400&ATCLID=206473761 |archive-date=November 3, 2013 }}</ref> Following the 2012–13 season he opted for the NBA draft, thereby forgoing his senior year of eligibility (though by that time he had already received his bachelor's degree in [[accounting]]).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gozags.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/041913aaa.html|title=Kelly Olynyk Announces Plans To Enter NBA Draft Early|work=GoZags.com|date=April 19, 2013|access-date=April 19, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180202071610/http://www.gozags.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/041913aaa.html|archive-date=February 2, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Nicole|last=Auerbach|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2013/04/19/gonzagas-kelly-olynyk-declares-for-nba-draft-after-breakout-year/2097545/|title=Gonzaga's Kelly Olynyk declares for NBA draft after breakout year|work=USA Today|date=April 19, 2013|access-date=May 17, 2013}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Boston Celtics (2013–2017)===
In a draft-night swap, Olynyk was selected by the [[Dallas Mavericks]] with the 13th overall pick in the [[2013 NBA draft]] and then traded to the [[Boston Celtics]] for the rights to [[Lucas Nogueira]] and two future second round picks.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/062813-celtics-acquire-olynyk-iverson|title=Celtics Acquire Olynyk, Iverson|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=June 28, 2013|access-date=June 28, 2013}}</ref> On July 7, 2013, Olynyk signed his rookie scale contract with the Celtics.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/070713-celtics-sign-olynyk|title=Celtics Sign Olynyk|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=July 7, 2013|access-date=July 7, 2013}}</ref> Olynyk was selected alongside teammate [[Jared Sullinger]] on Team Webber for the 2014 [[Rising Stars Challenge]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2014/news/as.rising.stars/02/06/all-star-rising-stars-release/|title=Hometown star Davis is top pick for BBVA Compass Rising Stars Challenge|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=February 6, 2014|access-date=February 6, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161108200939/http://www.nba.com/2014/news/as.rising.stars/02/06/all-star-rising-stars-release/|archive-date=November 8, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> After averaging 8.7 points and 5.2 rebounds in 70 games in 2013–14, he was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie Team|NBA All-Rookie second team]].

On October 29, 2014, the Celtics exercised their third-year team option on Olynyk's rookie scale contract, extending the contract through the 2015–16 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-exercise-options-olynyk-sullinger-and-zeller|title=Celtics Exercise Options on Olynyk, Sullinger and Zeller|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=October 29, 2014|access-date=October 29, 2014}}</ref> On December 15, 2014, he scored a career-high 30 points in a 105–87 win over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Aaron|last=Bracy|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141215/BOSPHI/gameinfo.html|title=Olynyk scores 30 in Celtics' 105–87 win over 76ers|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=December 16, 2014|access-date=December 16, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141227232057/http://www.nba.com/games/20141215/BOSPHI/gameinfo.html|archive-date=December 27, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> On January 22, 2015, he injured his ankle after landing on the foot of [[Thomas Robinson (basketball)|Thomas Robinson]] in the fourth quarter of the Celtics' 90–89 win over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]. After being projected to return soon after the All-Star break, Olynyk didn't show signs of being ready to return, and subsequently missed 18 games. He returned to action on March 4 against the [[Utah Jazz]]. In game 4 of the first round of the 2015 NBA playoffs, against the Cleveland Cavaliers, while grappling, he injured Kevin Love's shoulder. Love did not play the rest of the 2015 playoffs.<ref>{{cite web|first=Gary|last=Washburn|url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/sports/2015/03/05/kelly-olynyk-ankle-returns-celtics-after-game-absence/3Vo66wws5kJU0Ginj8cKBM/story.html|title=Kelly Olynyk (ankle) returns after 18-game absence|work=The Boston Globe|date=March 5, 2015|access-date=March 5, 2015}}</ref>

Olynyk missed the Celtics' 2015–16 season opener against the Philadelphia 76ers on October 28 after being suspended for his role in [[Kevin Love]]'s left shoulder injury during the 2015 playoffs.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/celtics-kelly-olynyk-suspended-for-season-opener/|title=Celtics' Kelly Olynyk: Suspended for season opener|work=CBSSports.com|date=October 28, 2015|access-date=October 28, 2015}}</ref> Two days later, the Celtics exercised their fourth-year team option on Olynyk's rookie scale contract, extending the contract through the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/Celtics-Exercise-Options-on%20Smart-Young-Olynyk|title=Celtics Exercise Options on Smart, Young & Olynyk|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=October 30, 2015|access-date=October 30, 2015}}</ref> On December 11, 2015, he scored a season-high 28 points in a 124–119 double overtime loss to the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Jimmy|last=Golen|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151211/GSWBOS/gameinfo.html|title=Curry, Warriors beat Boston 124–119 in 2OT, improve to 24–0|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=December 12, 2015|access-date=December 12, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190416064723/https://www.nba.com/games/20151211/GSWBOS/gameinfo.html|archive-date=April 16, 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref> On March 16, 2016, he returned to action for the Celtics after missing the previous 12 games with an injured right shoulder.<ref>{{cite web|first=Ken|last=Powtak|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160316/OKCBOS/gameinfo.html|title=Durant's 28 points leads Thunder to 130–109 win over Celtics|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=March 16, 2016|access-date=March 16, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160317050013/http://www.nba.com/games/20160316/OKCBOS/gameinfo.html|archive-date=March 17, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Olynyk missed the first six games of the 2016–17 season after undergoing right shoulder surgery in May 2016, and subsequently spent a day with the [[Maine Red Claws]] of the [[NBA Development League]] in early November.<ref>{{cite web|author=Boston Celtics|url=https://twitter.com/celtics/status/794650413467373568|title=Kelly Olynyk & Demetrius Jackson were assigned...|via=Twitter|date=November 4, 2016|access-date=January 14, 2017}}</ref>{{Primary source inline|date=January 2024}} He made his season debut for the Celtics on November 9, 2016, playing 25 minutes and scoring two points in a 118–93 loss to the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899557|title=Porter scores career-best 34 as Wizards rout Celtics 118–93|publisher=ESPN|date=November 9, 2016|access-date=November 9, 2016}}</ref> On January 13, 2017, he set a new season high with 26 points in a 103–101 win over the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900018|title=Thomas steadies Celtics, Horford triumphant in return home|publisher=ESPN|date=January 13, 2017|access-date=January 14, 2017}}</ref> In Game 7 of Boston's second-round playoff series against the [[Washington Wizards]] on May 15, he scored 14 of his playoff career-high 26 points in the first 8:34 minutes of the fourth quarter, making five consecutive shots, to help the Celtics advance to the Eastern Conference Finals for the first time since 2012 with a 115–105 win and a 4–3 series victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400952532|title=Celtics power past Wizards in Game 7, 115–105|publisher=ESPN|date=May 15, 2017|access-date=May 15, 2017}}</ref>

On July 4, 2017, after he became a restricted free agent, the Celtics renounced their rights to Olynyk, thus resulting in him becoming an unrestricted free agent.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportsnet.ca/basketball/nba/celtics-allow-canadian-kelly-olynyk-become-free-agent/|title=Report: Celtics allow Canadian Kelly Olynyk to become free agent|work=SportsNet.ca|date=July 4, 2017|access-date=July 5, 2017}}</ref>

===Miami Heat (2017–2021)===
On July 7, 2017, Olynyk signed a four-year, $50 million contract with the [[Miami Heat]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-signs-kelly-olynyk|title=HEAT Signs Kelly Olynyk|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=July 7, 2017|access-date=July 7, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=McKenna|first=Henry|url=http://www.csnne.com/boston-celtics/boston-celtics-report-kelly-olynyk-heat-agree-4-year-50-million-deal|title=Report: Kelly Olynyk, Heat Agree To 3-Year, $90 Million Deal|work=csnne.com|date=July 6, 2017|access-date=July 7, 2017}}</ref> In his debut for the Heat in their season opener on October 18, 2017, Olynyk scored 10 points in a 116–109 loss to the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974702|title=Fournier, Magic hold off Heat 116–109 in opener|publisher=ESPN|date=October 18, 2017|access-date=October 18, 2017}}</ref> On December 20, 2017, he scored a career-high 32 points in a 90–89 win over his former team, the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975207|title=Olynyk scores career-high 32 for Heat in return to Boston|publisher=ESPN|date=December 20, 2017|access-date=December 20, 2017}}</ref> On March 19, 2018, he scored 30 points off the bench in a 149–141 double-overtime win over the [[Denver Nuggets]], becoming the second bench player in Heat history to score 30 points.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975800|title=Stats system crashes in Miami as Heat top Nuggets in double overtime|publisher=ESPN|date=March 19, 2018|access-date=March 19, 2018}}</ref> Two days later, he recorded 22 points and a career-high 10 assists in a 119–98 win over the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975814|title=Olynyk's big night helps Heat past Knicks, 119–98|publisher=ESPN|date=March 21, 2018|access-date=March 22, 2018}}</ref>

On February 10, 2020, Olynyk recorded a double-double, which was 12 points and a new career-high 11 assists, along with six rebounds, one steal and one block in a 113–101 win against the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fantasypros.com/nba/news/250741/kelly-olynyk-dishes-out-season-high-11-assists-win.php|title=Kelly Olynyk dishes out season-high 11 assists in win|work=FantasyPros.com|date=February 11, 2020|access-date=March 2, 2020}}</ref> Olynyk helped the Heat reach the [[2020 NBA Finals]], where they lost to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in six games.

===Houston Rockets (2021)===
On March 25, 2021, Olynyk, [[Avery Bradley]], and a 2022 draft pick swap were traded to the [[Houston Rockets]] in exchange for [[Victor Oladipo]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-complete-trade-miami|title=Rockets Complete Trade with Miami|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=March 25, 2021}}</ref> Olynyk made his debut in a win over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] on March 27, recording 16 points, four rebounds, and four assists in 25 minutes.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Rockets' Kelly Olynyk: Scores 16 in Rockets debut|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/rockets-kelly-olynyk-scores-16-in-rockets-debut/|access-date=April 9, 2021|website=CBSSports.com|date=March 28, 2021 |language=en}}</ref> On April 27, he logged a season-high 28 points, alongside nine rebounds, five assists and two steals, in a 107–114 loss to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves|Timberwolves]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Timberwolves Beat Rockets 114–107 For Third Straight Win |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000931 |access-date=January 22, 2023 |publisher=National Basketball Association}}</ref>

===Detroit Pistons (2021–2022)===
On August 6, 2021, Olynyk signed a 3-year, $37 million contract with the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/features/detroit-pistons-sign-free-agents-kelly-olynyk-trey-lyles-and-restricted-free-agent-saben|title=Detroit Pistons Sign Free Agents Kelly Olynyk, Trey Lyles and Restricted Free Agent Saben Lee|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=August 6, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Report: Pistons signing Kelly Olynyk for three years, $37 million |url=https://nba.nbcsports.com/2021/08/02/report-pistons-signing-kelly-olynyk-for-three-years-37-million/ |access-date=March 12, 2022 |website=NBC Sports|date=August 2, 2021 }}</ref> On November 10, in a 112–104 win over the [[Houston Rockets]], he suffered a knee injury.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Grant has season-high 35 points, Pistons top Rockets 112–104 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401359986 |access-date=March 21, 2021 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref> Two days later, the injury was diagnosed as a grade 2 [[medial collateral ligament]] (MCL) sprain, ruling Olynyk out of action for at least six weeks.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pistons' Kelly Olynyk out at Least 6 Weeks with Knee Injury Diagnosed as MCL Sprain |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10015464-pistons-kelly-olynyk-out-at-least-6-weeks-with-knee-injury-diagnosed-as-mcl-sprain |access-date=March 21, 2022 |website=Bleacher Report}}</ref>

===Utah Jazz (2022–2024)===
On September 26, 2022, Olynyk was traded, alongside [[Saben Lee]], to the [[Utah Jazz]] in exchange for [[Bojan Bogdanović]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Angie|last=Treasure|title=Utah Jazz Acquire Kelly Olynyk, Saben Lee, and Cash Considerations|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-acquire-kelly-olynyk-saben-lee-and-cash-considerations|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=September 26, 2022|access-date=September 27, 2022}}</ref> On October 23, Olynyk put up 20 points, including the game-winning layup, in a 122–121 win over the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/jazz-news-kelly-olynyk-stuns-pelicans-with-ot-game-winner/|title=Jazz's Kelly Olynyk stuns Pelicans with OT game-winner|website=ClutchPoints|last=Villas|first=Rexwell|date=October 23, 2022|access-date=October 23, 2022}}</ref>

===Toronto Raptors (2024–2025)===
On February 8, 2024, Olynyk was traded to his hometown team the [[Toronto Raptors]] alongside [[Ochai Agbaji]] in exchange for [[Kira Lewis Jr.]], [[Otto Porter Jr.]], and a 2024 first-round draft pick<ref>{{cite web|title=Raptors Acquire Olynyk And Agbaji From Jazz|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-acquire-olynyk-and-agbaji-from-jazz|website=NBA.com|date=February 8, 2024|access-date=February 8, 2024}}</ref> and on March 4, he signed a two-year, $26.25 million extension with the Raptors.<ref>{{cite web|title=Raptors Extend Olynyk|url= https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-extend-olynyk|website=NBA.com|date=March 4, 2024|access-date=March 4, 2024}}</ref>

===New Orleans Pelicans (2025)===
On February 6, 2025, the Raptors traded Olynyk, [[Bruce Brown (basketball)|Bruce Brown]] and multiple draft picks to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] in exchange for [[Brandon Ingram]].<ref>{{cite web|title=New Orleans Pelicans complete trade with Toronto Raptors|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/new-orleans-pelicans-trade-toronto-raptors-nba-trade-deadline-brandon-ingram-february-6-2025|website=NBA.com|date=February 6, 2025}}</ref> In 20 starts for the Pelicans, he averaged 10.7 points, 5.9 rebounds, and 3.6 assists. On April 28, the Pelicans announced that Olynyk had undergone surgery on his left heel and an [[ultrasound]]-guided tendon [[debridement]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=New Orleans Pelicans center Kelly Olynyk, guard Brandon Boston undergo surgery|url=https://www.nola.com/sports/pelicans/pelicans-kelly-olynyk-brandon-boston-undergo-surgery/article_7245346d-82f9-4789-9485-3987265d8403.html|access-date=May 6, 2025|website=nola.com|language=en}}</ref>

===San Antonio Spurs (2025–2026)===
On July 6, 2025, Olynyk was traded to the [[Washington Wizards]] as part of a three-team trade that also included the Houston Rockets.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-complete-three-team-trade-2|title=Wizards Complete Three-Team Trade|publisher=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2025|access-date=July 7, 2025}}</ref> On July 9, Olynyk was traded to the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in exchange for [[Malaki Branham]], [[Blake Wesley (basketball)|Blake Wesley]], and a 2026 second-round draft pick.<ref>{{cite web|title=Spurs Acquire Kelly Olynyk|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-aquire-kelly-olynyk|website=NBA.com|date=July 9, 2025|access-date=July 9, 2025}}</ref>

==National team career==
On July 17, 2019, Olynyk was included on the [[Canada men's national basketball team|Canadian national team]]'s training camp roster,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2019/news/barrett-murray-olynyk-and-thompson-headline-canada-s-preliminary-squad-for-world-cup|title=Barrett, Murray, Olynyk and Thompson headline Canada's preliminary squad for World Cup|date=July 17, 2019|website=fiba.basketball|access-date=July 17, 2019}}</ref> but withdrew from the team after being injured in an exhibition game with [[Nigeria national basketball team|Nigeria]] on August 7.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/kelly-olynyk-injury-update|title=Kelly Olynyk Injury Update|date=August 14, 2019|publisher=National Basketball Association|access-date=August 14, 2019}}</ref>

On May 24, 2022, Olynyk agreed to a three-year commitment to play with the Canadian senior men's national team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fourteen Athletes Committed To Represent Canada As Senior Men's National Team Summer Core Revealed |url=https://www.basketball.ca/news/athletes-committed-to-represent-canada-as-senior-mens-national-team-summer-core-revealed |access-date=May 24, 2022 |website=Canada Basketball}}</ref> He was named captain of Canada's team for the [[Basketball at the 2024 Summer Olympics|2024 Summer Olympics in Paris]].<ref>{{cite web| title = Gilgeous-Alexander, Murray to lead NBA-experienced Canadian Olympic team in Paris| publisher = CBC / The Canadian Press | url = https://www.cbc.ca/sports/olympics/summer/basketball/canada-olympic-mens-basketball-roster-paris-1.7259301 | access-date = July 10, 2014}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Olynyk is of [[Ukrainian Canadians|Ukrainian]] descent.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 5, 2022 |title=6 Ukrainian Canadian athletes you should know |url=https://www.cbc.ca/kids/articles/6-ukrainian-canadian-athletes-you-should-know |access-date=October 17, 2025 |website=CBC Kids}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Orlando|first=Aaron|url=http://www.revelstokereview.com/sports/200533431.html|title=Kelly Olynyk family, sports success rooted in Revelstoke|work=revelstokereview.com|date=March 28, 2013|access-date=January 14, 2017|archive-date=May 5, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170505201113/http://www.revelstokereview.com/sports/200533431.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> 

Olynyk's mother, [[Arlene Olynyk]], played college basketball for the [[Lethbridge Pronghorns]] and was a [[U Sports|Canadian Interuniversity Sport]] (CIS; now U Sports) women's basketball referee.<ref name="toronto" /><ref name="Anderson" /> From 1995 to 2004, she worked for the [[Toronto Raptors]] as the NBA’s first female scorekeeper and was the scorekeeper for the Toronto Raptors' first-ever regular season game on November 3, 1995, against the [[Brooklyn Nets|New Jersey Nets]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Canadian NBA player Kelly Olynyk grew up around Raptors as mom made history as team's scorekeeper | website=CBC | date=2020-11-02 | url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/basketball/nba/kelly-olynyk-toronto-raptors-25th-anniversary-1.5776082 | access-date=2025-12-13}}</ref> His father, [[Ken Olynyk]], was the head coach of the [[Lethbridge Pronghorns]] men's basketball team from 1979 to 1988 and the [[Toronto Varsity Blues]] men's basketball team from 1989 to 2002, as well as the [[Canada men's national under-19 basketball team|Canada junior men's national basketball team]] from 1983 to 1996, notably cutting future Canadian basketball icon [[Steve Nash]] from the team.<ref name="Anderson" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Woodard |first=Dale |date=January 14, 2025 |title=Pronghorn Athletics Announces Ken Olynyk as 2025 Pronghorns Hall of Fame Inductee |url=https://gohorns.ca/news/2025/1/14/mens-basketball-pronghorn-athletics-announces-ken-olynyk-as-2025-pronghorns-hall-of-fame-inductee.aspx |access-date=October 17, 2025 |website=University of Lethbridge Athletics}}</ref> In 2003, Ken became the athletic director at [[Thompson Rivers WolfPack|Thompson Rivers University]] in [[Kamloops]], [[British Columbia]], with the rest of the family soon joining him in Kamloops.<ref name="Anderson" /><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.tru.ca/athletics/history/history.html |title=Athletics History |publisher=[[Thompson Rivers University]] |access-date=March 23, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130315070152/http://www.tru.ca/athletics/history/history.html |archive-date=March 15, 2013 }}</ref> Olynyk has two sisters, Jesse and Maya; Jesse has represented Canada in both wrestling and rugby, while Maya has played CIS basketball for the [[Saskatchewan Huskies]].
